title: Burns and scalds
description: Damage to skin and tissue from heat (fire, hot liquid, steam, hot object), electricity, or chemicals.

recognition_questions.q: What caused the burn (heat, hot liquid, chemical, electricity)?
Is the burn larger than the person's palm, or on the face/hands/genitals/major joints?
Is the person having trouble breathing?

immediate_safety_warnings: Ensure the source of heat is off and the person is moved away from danger (fire, electricity, chemical).
Do not approach a person still in contact with electricity without switching off the power.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Move the person away from the source of the burn safely.
Cool the burn immediately with cool (not ice-cold) running water for 20 minutes.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Cooling stops the burn progressing and relieves pain.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Remove jewellery, watches, and tight clothing near the burn before it swells — but NOT if clothing is stuck to the burn.
Cover the burn loosely with cling film or a clean, non-fluffy cloth.
Call 112 for large burns, facial burns, electrical burns, chemical burns, or burns to a child or infant.

actions_to_avoid: Do not use ice or very cold water — it can deepen the injury.
Do not apply toothpaste, butter, oil, herbs, or any home remedy.
Do not peel off clothing stuck to the burn.
Do not apply adhesive dressings directly to the burn.

escalation_conditions.condition: Burn larger than the palm of the hand
Burn to face, hands, genitals, feet, or major joints

escalation_conditions.action: Call 112; brush dry chemicals off before flushing; flush liquid chemicals for 20+ minutes

escalation_conditions.condition: Person not breathing after a fire

equipment_requirements.item: Cling film or clean non-fluffy cloth

approved_alternatives.alternative: Clean damp cotton cloth, kept wet
Cool water in a clean container if no tap available

follow_up_requirements: All but minor burns need medical assessment.

age_specific_pathways.child: Children have thinner skin — burns are more severe than they appear. Seek medical advice for any burn in a child.
age_specific_pathways.infant: All infant burns need urgent medical assessment.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
